headline: Reviewing bone age
punch: Where the number actually comes from.

headline: Basic Understanding:
body: Bone age is read from a hand and wrist X-ray, then applied to your whole skeleton. There is a common assumption that all your plates are at the same stage. However, that is simply not true. | Your hand and your legs are on different timelines, and the hand is the one that finishes first.
punch: Your hand is not where your height comes from.

headline: Dolan et al
subhead: (TLDR SO YOU CAN PLACE IT IN YOUR MAP)
body: In mice, *epiphyseal fusion* happened at **3 weeks** in phalanges and **4 weeks** in metacarpals, tibia and femur still open at **12 weeks**. Rats, same order: **12** and **16** weeks vs still open. | Key identity I would assign the hand bones: early closer, slow grower, first to senesce.

headline: Rate
subhead: THE HAND RUNS AT HALF SPEED
body: At one week the metacarpal growth rate was **49%** of the tibial rate and *proliferation per column* was **46%**. Every marker of *growth plate senescence*, the plate running out of divisions, was more advanced in the hand bones. | So the hand is not just earlier. It sits further along the same curve at every age.
punch: ==Your hand bones grow at half the speed of your legs.==

headline: Mechanism
body: *Chondrocytes* from finger bones proliferated slower than leg bone chondrocytes. Add IGF-1 to the finger cells and proliferation rose **to match the untreated leg cells**. | Right in the middle of the whole story: same cells, less signal. That is the entire difference.
punch: The bone is the same. The signal is not.

headline: Kvist 2021
body: Wrist, knee and ankle imaged in **958 people** aged 14 to 21. Fusion timing varied by site inside the same person, complete fusion about **2 years earlier** in girls. | *Pubertal stage* correlated with fusion at every site, **0.514 to 0.598** in males. This is the variable you want to track.

headline: Training vs BMI
body: **BMI correlated** with plate maturity, 0.186 to 0.384. **Physical activity**: no significant correlation in males at any site, one very low correlation at the female wrist (**0.095**), nothing else. | There is a common take that training closes your plates. However, in the largest human imaging study on this, it barely registered.
punch: ==Being heavier tracked faster maturation. Training did not.==

headline: Verdict
body: Bone age = estimate from your fastest ageing bones, not your legs. Track pubertal stage. And the hand finishes first, always.
